response: The Canada's Compassionate Care Benefit (CCB) is not an adequate public health response to addressing the issue of caregiver burden in end-of-life care. According to a study, the CCB is not living up to its full potential in sustaining informal caregivers providing end-of-life care. Efforts are required to transform the CCB so that it can fulfill its potential and serve as a public health response to caregiver burden, as part of a healthy public policy that addresses the determinants of this burden. In other words, while the CCB is a step in the right direction, it needs significant improvements to effectively support family caregivers and alleviate the burden of end-of-life care.
